questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit safely under a bridge, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve as you pass under the bridge.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object, slow down. Find an alternate route if possible.

questions.question: What is a danger if your vehicle rolls backward when you start to accelerate?

options.text: The truck is not made to go backwards.
You may hit a vehicle behind you.
You may lose your position in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: You must prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop. This will avoid hitting someone or something behind you. If you have a manual transmission, partly engage the clutch before taking your foot off the brake.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you plan to slow down?

options.text: Tap the brakes a few times before braking.
Turn on one set of turn signals.
Put your hand out the driver's side window and wave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes a few times before braking.
questions.explanation: Before slowing down, lightly tap your brake pedal a few times. This flashes your brake lights and warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: After the engine starts, what should happen to warning lights and buzzers?

options.text: They should turn off right away.
They should turn off once the vehicle begins moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should turn off right away.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, all warning lights and buzzers should turn off immediately. This includes the charging circuit warning, oil, coolant, and Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) lights.

questions.question: Where do bus accidents happen most often?
questions.explanation: Bus accidents happen most often at intersections. Be extra careful when driving where there are many vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: In bad weather, what do many drivers like to do?
questions.explanation: In bad weather with poor visibility, many drivers follow trucks closely. Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you if someone is following you too closely.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, the landing gear should be:

options.text: More worn on the passenger's side than on the driver's side.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a trailer, check that the landing gear is fully raised with no missing parts. The crank handle should be secure and the support frame should not be damaged.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When there is a lot of traffic.
When vehicles are too close to one another.

questions.explanation: A rollover happens when a driver changes lanes or turns too quickly.

questions.question: If a bus has a restroom, what must be included?
questions.explanation: A bus restroom must have an emergency buzzer.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, what should you check on the hoses?

options.text: To ensure they are still clear.
To ensure they are connected to the battery.
To ensure they have the proper amount of play.

questions.explanation: When inspecting power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look specifically for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving and finish your trip.

questions.explanation: Sleep is the only real way to fix drowsiness while driving. Coffee and other drugs may help you stay awake for a short time, but you will become even more tired when the drug wears off.

questions.question: When driving on the expressway during a skills test, you should:

options.text: Use your mirrors to check traffic regularly.
Stay on the left side of your lane.
Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check traffic regularly.
questions.explanation: During a driving skills test on the expressway, keep a safe distance from other vehicles and drive at the posted speed limit. Check your mirrors and look around you in all directions.

questions.question: What is the smallest size allowed for a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be diamond-shaped and at least 10 ¾ square inches.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you remember?

options.text: You can usually drive across before a train arrives.
Do not rely only on warning lights and gates.
Roll down a window to listen for a train.
Only check the closest track to your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on warning lights and gates.
questions.explanation: Never trust only warning signals to tell you a train is coming. Never try to race a train across the tracks. If there are multiple tracks, look both ways on all tracks before crossing.

questions.question: What maneuver may be included in a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include these maneuvers: backing in a straight line, backing into spaces from the side, parallel parking on the driver side, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When merging back into traffic after stopping, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will let you in.
Wait for a large enough gap so you can speed up and safely merge.
Have a passenger direct traffic to let you in.
Keep honking until other drivers let you in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large enough gap so you can speed up and safely merge.
questions.explanation: Be aware of how fast your vehicle accelerates and how much space it takes on the road. Always wait for a gap in traffic that is big enough for your vehicle before you pull out from a stop.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the roadway:

options.text: Could hold a heavy object that damages your vehicle.
Should be avoided by driving off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Could hold a heavy object that damages your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is potentially dangerous. Something that looks harmless, like a cardboard box, could hide a hard or heavy object that could seriously damage your vehicle.

questions.question: When a bus approaches a railroad crossing, how can the driver better hear a train?

options.text: Wait for passengers to be quiet.
Tell passengers to get off and check the tracks.

questions.explanation: When stopped at a railroad crossing, a bus driver should open the front door if it helps them see or hear a train coming.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, why should a driver look under the vehicle?

options.text: To see if the vehicle is parked on a hill.
To check for fresh fluid leaks.
To see if the vehicle is in a parking spot.
To see if the vehicle is parked downhill.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check for fresh fluid leaks.
questions.explanation: Before starting your vehicle, look underneath it for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks on the ground. Leaks mean the vehicle has unsafe problems.

questions.question: A stopped bus on the roadway:

options.text: Is safe if no passengers are getting off.
Should not be on the roadway.
Is a safety concern in all situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a safety concern in all situations.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front or behind the bus, and the bus may block them from your view.
